ATAX: y update has reduction over i. Common optimization: fuse the two j loops per i, parallelize over i with private y? Actually y is shared reduction. Standard approach: parallelize over i, each thread accumulates into private y buffer, then reduce. Or restructure: compute tmp[i] in parallel, then y[j] += A[i][j]*tmp[i] with parallel over j per i — race on y across i. Better: parallel over i with private local y array, then critical/atomic merge. Simpler: parallel for over i, tmp[i] computed, then inner j loop updating y with atomic — slow. Use per-thread local y and reduction at end.

Implement:

#pragma scop
for i y[i]=0;
#pragma omp parallel private(local_y)
init local_y to 0;
#pragma omp for schedule(static)
for i: tmp[i]=sum; for j: local_y[j]+=A[i][j]*tmp[i];
#pragma omp for reduction(+:y[:N])? OpenMP array reduction supported in 4.5: reduction(+:y[0:_PB_N]) — but y is a pointer (POLYBENCH_1D). Array section on pointer works. But reduction on array sections requires... it's valid OpenMP 4.5. Alternatively manual merge with critical over chunks. Use reduction(+:y[:_PB_N])? _PB_N macro — fine.

But reduction on array sections may not be universally supported; safer: merge loop with #pragma omp for and atomic per element — slow. Use critical with static chunk merge:

#pragma omp for schedule(static)
for (j=0;j<N;j++) — no, each thread has local_y only for its i-range; merging needs thread's local_y. Do:

each thread after its i-loop merges its local_y into y under critical. But omp for splits i; thread knows its range? Not easily. Alternative: use omp parallel with explicit manual partitioning:

#pragma omp parallel
{
  allocate local_y (VLA DATA_TYPE local_y[_PB_N]) — stack ok.
  init to 0.
  #pragma omp for schedule(static) nowait
  for i: compute tmp[i], update local_y.
  #pragma omp critical
  for j: y[j]+=local_y[j];
}

With static schedule, each thread's i-range contiguous; merge under critical is fine. That's correct and fast. Need y initialized before parallel region (keep first loop, maybe parallelize too).
